rules.message: agent-policy: this NixOS system is declarative. Use an ephemeral 'nix shell nixpkgs#<pkg> --command ...' for one-off needs.

agent-policy: a Python library supplied as a separate 'nix shell' installable is not added to the interpreter's sys.path. Compose one environment instead; this works in repositories without a flake: nix shell --impure --expr 'let pkgs = (builtins.getFlake "nixpkgs").legacyPackages.${builtins.currentSystem}; in pkgs.python312.withPackages (ps: [ ps.<package> ])' --command python ... . Here --impure permits host registry and system lookup; use a pinned flake for shared scripts or CI.

agent-policy: sleeping before or between CI status reads guesses a duration and then burns tokens re-reading. Block on the real signal, which also sets the exit code: gh pr checks <pr> --watch --fail-fast, or gh run watch <run-id> --exit-status. For several PRs, watch them concurrently and wait: for n in 1 2 3; do gh pr checks $n --watch --fail-fast & done; wait

agent-policy: a traversal rooted at / or the nix store enumerates an enormous tree. Resolve instead: readlink -f "$(command -v <bin>)" for a binary's store path; nix eval nixpkgs#<pkg>.outPath for a package; nix-locate <file> for file-to-package. Otherwise pick a reasoned, specific root — and if a broad scan is truly unavoidable, bound it hard: timeout 5 <cmd> ... with a -maxdepth.

agent-policy: recursive grep from / or the nix store reads an enormous tree. Resolve the location first (readlink -f, nix eval, nix-locate), then search a reasoned root — and if a broad scan is truly unavoidable, bound it hard: timeout 5 grep ... with a narrower root.

agent-policy: /mnt/* paths are slow network/Windows mounts where every directory read is a round trip. Bound any search there hard — a few seconds already covers enormous ground: timeout 5 <cmd> ... with -maxdepth 3 or less from a deep, specific root (e.g. timeout 5 find /mnt/<share>/<dir> -maxdepth 2 -iname '*<term>*'), or ls the target directory first to orient.

agent-policy: this cd targets a slow network/Windows mount and the script then walks the filesystem. Bound the search hard: timeout 5 <cmd> ... with -maxdepth 3 or less, or ls the target directory first to orient.

agent-policy: inside a git repository, query the index first: git ls-files '*<name>*', or fd/rg which honor .gitignore. Raw find must bound its walk: -not -path '*/.venv/*' -not -path '*/node_modules/*', a -prune, or a -maxdepth.

agent-policy: excluding .git still walks it first -- the exclusion hides output, not the traversal. Single repo: git -C <dir> ls-files or grep reads the index directly. Directory of many repos: rg --files or fd walk once, skipping every nested .git and each repo's own .gitignore. For a deliberately ignored or untracked target, ls-files shows nothing -- use git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard or git check-ignore -v <path>.

agent-policy: piping through grep -v or rg -v to drop .git/ lines still walks .git first -- the filter hides output, not the traversal. Single repo: git -C <dir> ls-files. Directory of many repos: rg --files or fd. Deliberately untracked target: git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard.
